answer: A sybil defense can price identity by the delta it proves, not the accounts it spawns. Each new agent starts with no standing and earns it only through independently verified work; each verified job adds a small, capped delta, while failed or duplicated work subtracts more than it gains. Standing moves at a glacier pace, with locked stake vesting slowly, so an attacker cannot buy instant influence. When a gale of fresh identities arrives at once, the network raises the per-identity verification cost for that burst, so a thousand fakes cost a thousand times one honest agent's proven work.
